Footer Bar

The site footer bar: company menu, review badges, brand and address, socials, partner logos and the legal line. It sits below Product Footer — the two stack, they do not replace each other.

3 of 3 variants3 bands1440 · 768 · 375◆ Dark onlyFigma 877:2953

Default

Figma’s Property 1=Default. The menu row and the brand row are both --color-bg-footer-alt; only the legal row underneath is --color-bg-footer — the opposite way round to what the token names suggest.

The panel animates with grid-template-rows: 0fr → 1fr, so it opens to whatever height its own content needs — no measured max-height to go stale when a link is added. Each column then rises in turn, and prefers-reduced-motion collapses all of it to a cut. Collapsed, the panel carries inert: it stays in the DOM to animate, and inert is what stops it from holding focus while it is closed.

Responsive

Figma draws footer-md (768) and footer-sm (375) as separate symbols. They are mapped onto this project’s own breakpoints — --breakpoint-lg 1024 and --breakpoint-md 768 — so the wide layout holds down to 1024, md covers 768–1023 and sm everything below. Those numbers are written out in the @media conditions rather than read from the tokens, because a custom property in a media query condition never matches.
Each preview below is an <iframe> loading this same page at ?frame=, because an iframe is the only thing on a page with a viewport of its own — the demo frames above are pinned to 1440 and will never show these. Nothing is duplicated to make them work.
768px
Drag the handle, or use the presets — the readout names the layout you are looking at, and the frame reports its own height back so nothing is a guessed number. The handle takes arrow keys too (±16, or ±1 with Shift), which is worth having: dragging to find the exact pixel where a layout flips is how you check a breakpoint landed where you meant it to. The menu drops its per-item padding for a flat 12px gap and wraps — two rows at 768, three at 375, matching Figma’s wrap points exactly. The Free tools panel has no frame to match: its groups stack, and inside each one the design’s editorial column breaks stay intact while auto-fill decides how many sit per row — 4 at 768, 2 at 375, 1 at 320.
